action.action-desc: Mr. Donalds introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce

form.official-title: To require that new and existing data centers use off-grid power and water supplies, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Protecting Ratepayers Act.

paragraph.text: The term covered entity means a private company, or other private entity, that—

subparagraph.text: owns, operates, or maintains a data center; or
has plans to own, operate, or maintain a data center within the next 5 years.

paragraph.text: The term data center means a data center, as defined in section 453(a) of the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 (42 U.S.C. 17112(a)), with a power demand of 5 megawatts or more.
The term existing data center means a data center that has begun operations as of the date of enactment of this Act.
The term new data center means a data center or planned data center that is not yet operational as of the date of enactment of this Act.

section.header: Data center requirement for off-grid power and water supply
section.text: Beginning on the date that is 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, a covered entity may not build, own, operate, or maintain a new data center or existing data center unless the data center derives all—

paragraph.text: energy, including back-up energy, from a captive power plant, on-site power generation, or some other source or combination of sources separate from, and not deriving power from, the electric grid; and
water, including back-up water, from an on-site water source, or some other water source or combination of sources separate from, and not deriving water from, the public water system.

section.text: Proclamation of the President issued on March 9, 2026, titled Ratepayer Protection Pledge (91 Fed. Reg. 11439) shall have the full force and effect of law.
